newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. state senator says Pataki inflates job growth.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. state senator says Pataki inflates job growth.

text.p: A New York State Senator on Tuesday accused Governor George Pataki of inflating his success in creating new jobs, saying the former Cuomo administration generated almost twice as many jobs in its final 20 months.

"Instead of generating growth, his (Pataki's) costly tax cuts and generous subsidies and tax breaks for businesses have slowed the state's economic recovery," said Franz Leichter, D-Manhattan, in prepared remarks.
The state senator said that Pataki had produced a net gain of 59,500 jobs when measured on a statewide basis, for a 0.75 percent growth rate, in his first 20 months in office.
But Leichter added that former governor Mario Cuomo, a Democrat, was responsible for a net gain of 117,400 jobs for a 1.5 percent growth rate during his final 20 months in office.

A spokeswoman for the Empire State Development Corp said that Pataki disputed the senator's findings. Caroline Quartarao quoted the governor as saying that since he took office an average of 5,000 jobs a month were created.
She also quoted Pataki as saying the same number of jobs was lost each month under the Cuomo administration.
"Senator Franz Leichter is probably the only senator left on the earth who thinks raising taxes promotes economic growth. He's been wrong before and he's wrong again," she said.
